_source: Transcribed from the GWMS Curriculum Guide in Notion, rebuilt September 26, 2026 for the three-games model. Game fields (games array) come from each session's Grappling Class Guide (Unit 7), Start 1 of each of the three CVP games, with the GWMS Game Rulings applied. TLO/ELO/connection/takeaway come from each session's Lesson and Intervention Guide. Nothing here is authored beyond plain-language rewording of the guides' own words.

stage.name: The Initiation
stage.grapplingTlo: By the end of the Initiation, participants will apply chest-pin control and its owned finishes to make contact, hold it under resistance, and reset cleanly after a break, releasing on every tap.
stage.caselTlo: By the end of the Initiation, participants will apply social awareness and relationship skills to make real contact with others, tolerate friction, own their part in a rupture, and attempt repair.
stage.connection: Chest-to-chest contact on the mat is like contact with people. Friction on the mat is like friction with people. A break on the mat is like a rupture between people. A reset on the mat is like repair between people. The Initiation tests the real you against other people.

wrongAnswers.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
wrongAnswers.feedback: Never. Let go the instant he taps.

sessions.probingQuestion: What happens in you when someone makes real contact?

games.title: Standing Hand Connection Game
games.start: Both players stand in an even position, each with an underhook.
games.text: Fight to get under your partner's elbows. Make a closed-hand connection anywhere from armpits to ankles.

win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Chest-to-Chest via Outside Line Only
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is standing.
games.text: Top player: touch a knee pit first, then get to the outside of both legs, one then the other, and stay outside. Only then close in with chest contact and connect your hands around the bottom player. Bottom player: hook and post to make the top player sit down, then sit up.

win.text: wins by connecting his hands around the bottom player from the outside.
wins by making the top player's butt hit the mat and sitting up.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Chest to Chest Under Elbows Maintenance
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest, both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: keep both elbows away from the bottom player's body, using any body part in place of your arms if you need to. Bottom player: get both elbows back to touch your own body, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps both elbows covered.
wins by getting both elbows to touch his body, or by making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player gets both elbows to his body, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: Holding contact on the mat and noticing what contact does to you are the same skill. Both mean staying present when someone gets close, instead of pushing them away. The pin teaches your body to stay. Thinking about it teaches your mind why staying is hard.
sessions.takeaway: Contact does something to all of us. Now you can feel yours.

sessions.probingQuestion: How much of someone else do you actually let in?

games.title: Role-Based Consecutive Touch vs Close Hand Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range. One is the touch player, one is the connection player.
games.text: Touch player: collect three touches in a row, a hand to the mat or a hand behind the knee, without letting the connection player close his hands on you. If he scores, your count goes back to zero. Connection player: close both hands around the touch player anywhere from armpits to ankles.

win.text: wins with three touches in a row.
wins with a closed-hand connection from armpits to ankles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Closed Guard Hand Fighting Game
games.start: The bottom player has closed guard around the top player, who is on his knees inside, trying to open it.
games.text: Bottom player: keep your hands on the top player, connecting to his wrists, elbows, and head to make his hands touch the mat once. Top player: take your hands off the bottom player and get to your feet.

win.text: wins by making the top player's hands touch the mat one time.
wins by getting his hands off the bottom player and standing up.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Chest-to-Chest Elbow Control Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest, both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: stay under the bottom player's elbows, keeping them away from his body. Bottom player: get both elbows to touch your body, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: wins by keeping the elbows away from the body the whole time.
wins by bringing both elbows to his body, or by making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player gets both elbows to his body, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: Keeping a pin means feeling your partner and adjusting to them, not clamping down and ignoring them. Letting someone in works the same way. You hold the connection by reading the other person, not by shutting them out and pushing through alone.
sessions.takeaway: Letting people in is like a dial you control. You just found yours.

sessions.probingQuestion: Who are you with other people, now that you've met yourself?

games.title: Hand Fight to Connection Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both disconnected.
games.text: Get a two-on-one connection, then the underhook, and work to a connection at the head, waist, or leg.

win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Closed Guard, Post to Underhook to Locked Hands
games.start: The bottom player has closed guard around the top player, who may work to standing.
games.text: Bottom player: attach to the wrists and elbows to cause a post, get the underhook on that post, then lock your hands around a shoulder. Top player: keep your hands on the bottom player and fight to stand up with the guard open.

win.text: wins by locking his hands with an underhook after a post.
wins by standing and opening the guard.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Mount, Stay Under Both Elbows
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is in mount with both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: stay under at least one elbow the whole round. If you lose one, fight to get it back. Bottom player: get both elbows to touch your own body with nothing under them, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps at least one elbow covered.
wins by touching both elbows to his body, or by making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If he loses both elbows, that is the bottom player's win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: The Descent found the real you. Now it goes to the mat with a partner. Rolling as the real you, instead of a mask, is the same as showing up honest in a relationship instead of performing one.
sessions.takeaway: The real you is in the room now, and other people are in it too.

sessions.probingQuestion: What do you do when someone pushes back?

games.title: Underhook Introduction Game
games.start: Both players stand. The underhook player has an underhook. The overhook player counters with an overhook.
games.text: Underhook player: use the underhook to move your partner and attach to a single leg, then pick it up. Overhook player: use the overhook to keep him away from that leg.

win.text: wins by attaching to and picking up the overhook player's leg.
wins by stopping him for 30 seconds.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Post and Hook Destabilization Game
games.start: Open guard. The bottom player is on his back. The top player is standing or kneeling in front of him.
games.text: Bottom player: use only posts and hooks, no leg entanglements and no attaching to the hips, to put the top player's hips on the floor. Top player: do not get put down. Work to pass or keep the top position.

win.text: wins by putting the top player's hips on the floor using only posts and hooks.
wins by stopping the bottom player's win for 30 seconds. Then you switch roles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Riding Bottom Position Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his hands and knees. The top player is on top with open hands around the bottom player's hips.
games.text: Top player: stay attached to the hips, break the bottom player down, and stop him from standing. Bottom player: build your base, fight to your feet, and turn to face the top player.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the bottom player broken down.
wins by standing up and turning to face the top player.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player stands and turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: A partner resisting the pin is pushback made physical. What you do when they fight the pin is usually what you do when people push back in life. Both reward staying calm and adjusting over forcing harder.
sessions.takeaway: Pushback is normal. Your response to it is a choice, not a reflex you're stuck with.

sessions.probingQuestion: Can you stay present when it gets uncomfortable?

games.title: Waist Control Leg Stuffing Game
games.start: Both players stand. The back player is behind, hands connected around the front player's waist.
games.text: Back player: keep your hands connected and move the front player around. Stuff one leg in front of his to put his hands on the mat. Front player: separate the hands and turn to face the back player.

win.text: wins when the front player's hands touch the mat.
wins by freeing himself and turning to face.

games.reset: This one runs without a break. Play continues until someone wins, then you switch roles.

games.title: Guard Recovery with Passing Resistance Game
games.start: The bottom player is lying on his side. The top player has passed the legs and is at his hips.
games.text: Bottom player: stay mobile on your side, stop the top player's hands from connecting, and get your legs back in front. Top player: lock your hands around the bottom player's waist, chest, or back to stop the recovery.

win.text: wins by recovering to any real guard position while staying mobile.
wins by locking his hands.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Rear Hip Connection, Keep Belly Down
games.start: The defender is on his elbows and knees. The attacker is behind him, hands locked around his waist.
games.text: Attacker: keep the defender belly down, using knee-to-knee and foot-to-foot blocking to pull his hips to the mat. Defender: rise to a quad pod, both knees and both elbows off the floor.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the defender belly down.
wins by reaching a quad pod.

games.reset: The attacker holds no matter what. If the defender reaches a quad pod, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: Staying in an uncomfortable pin instead of scrambling out is like staying in a hard conversation. Both take the same skill: putting up with discomfort instead of running from it.
sessions.note: Staying is the skill. But leaving a harmful situation is wise, not a failure.
sessions.takeaway: You can stay when things feel uncomfortable. You just did it.

sessions.probingQuestion: What does your friction do to the people across from you?

games.title: Foot-to-Foot Contact with Overhook / Underhook
games.start: Both players stand. The overhook player has an overhook. The underhook player has an underhook.
games.text: Overhook player: keep the overhook, use both hands to move your partner, and make foot-to-foot contact with either leg. Underhook player: close your hands anywhere below the overhook player's elbows and above his ankles.

win.text: wins when the underhook player falls to his hips or hands.
wins by closing his hands under the elbows.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Seated Open Guard Game
games.start: The top player stands. The bottom player sits on the mat with an inside hook and a knee-pit grip.
games.text: Bottom player: move from seated to belly up, using your connections to put the top player down on his hips or hands, then wrestle up or stand and make his back touch the mat. Top player: put the bottom player on his back and keep shin contact.

win.text: wins by standing up and reaching the hips, or by making the top player's back touch the mat.
wins with shin contact on the knees or body.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Figure Four Grip Control Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player covers his head with a figure-four grip, one hand on the wrist, the other arm under the elbow.
games.text: Top player: keep the figure-four grip and stay under at least one elbow while keeping the bottom player pinned. Bottom player: break the grip by freeing your arms and getting your elbows to your body.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the grip.
wins by breaking the grip.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player breaks the grip, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: You can pin someone hard and still keep them safe. That is control of your own force. Your conflict off the mat lands on real people too, and the same control applies: honest friction, not harm.
sessions.takeaway: Friction is fine. Harm is a choice. The control is yours.

sessions.probingQuestion: What breaks in you when a connection breaks?

games.title: Single Leg, Make Partner Fall to Hands or Hips
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker is connected to one of the defender's legs.
games.text: Attacker: move the defender using only that leg, run him, pull him, turn him, or lift him, to make his hips or hands touch the mat. Defender: stay balanced and use your connections to break the grip and free your leg.

win.text: wins when the defender's hips or hands touch the mat.
wins by freeing the leg.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Guard Recovery After Leg Pass Game
games.start: The bottom player is lying on his side. The top player has already passed the legs and is at his hips.
games.text: Bottom player: stay mobile on your side, control the top player's arms to stop his hands from locking, and get your legs back in front. Top player: lock your hands around the bottom player's body.

win.text: wins by getting his legs back in front in any real guard.
wins by locking his hands around the bottom player.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Figure Four Grip Control Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player covers his head with a figure-four grip, one hand on the wrist, the other arm under the elbow.
games.text: Top player: keep the figure-four grip and stay under at least one elbow while keeping the bottom player pinned. Bottom player: break the grip by freeing your arms and getting your elbows to your body.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the grip.
wins by breaking the grip.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player breaks the grip, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: Losing the pin and getting reversed is a small rupture. How you handle that break on the mat, a clean reset or payback, is a lot like how you handle broken connections in life.
sessions.takeaway: A rupture teaches you something. You survived naming it.

sessions.probingQuestion: Have you ever broken something with someone and left it broken?

games.title: Stick and Pull Foot Sweep Game
games.start: Both players stand. The overhook player has an overhook. The underhook player has an underhook.
games.text: Overhook player: move your partner, make foot-to-foot contact, then stick the foot and pull, with your foot, your upper body, or your hands, to put him on a knee or his back. Underhook player: connect your hands, then lift him fully off the ground, get behind him, or pick up a leg.

win.text: wins by putting the underhook player on a knee or his back.
wins by lifting him, getting behind him, or picking up a leg.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Closed Guard Opening, Hands on Body
games.start: The bottom player has closed guard locked around the top player. The top player is inside the guard, hands on him.
games.text: Top player: hold the bottom player down, get to your feet, and press on his hips, knees, and feet to open his legs. Bottom player: keep your legs closed, using only open-hand grips on the head, wrists, and elbows.

win.text: wins by getting to his feet and opening the guard.
wins by stopping the top player's win for 30 seconds. Then you switch roles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Head and Arm Strangle, Close Position Start
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is in mount, one hand under his head and one under his arm. No strangle is on yet.
games.text: Top player: bring the bottom player's arm to his head and trap it there, staying under at least one elbow the whole time. Bottom player: bring the trapped elbow back to your body with nothing between it, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: wins with the arm trapped at the head.
wins by touching that elbow to his body.

games.reset: The win is the trap, not the strangle. No finish is shown. The tap is honored instantly, every time. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the trap, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.

sessions.connection: A finish you can apply and release on the tap is power you control. Leaving a break unrepaired is choosing not to release, not to reset. The tap is the invitation to repair. This week asks whether you take it.
sessions.takeaway: Naming the break you never fixed is the first step toward repair.

sessions.probingQuestion: When something breaks, what part is yours to own?

games.title: Single Leg Destabilization, Two Paths
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker is connected on one of the defender's legs at the knee. The defender is in a single-leg defensive position.
games.text: Attacker: stay connected and move the defender around, then either work down to the ankle for a foot-to-foot takedown, or move to capture both legs together. Defender: use your connections to separate the attacker's hands and free yourself completely.

win.text: wins when the defender's hips or hands touch the mat.
wins by freeing himself completely.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Knee Pit Touchdown Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is standing and starts by clearing the feet.
games.text: Top player: clear the feet, then step one leg into one knee pit, then the other, keeping your feet off. Bottom player: hook and post with your feet, using your hands to make him hit his butt, then sit up.

win.text: wins by touching both knee pits with his leg while keeping his feet off.
wins by sitting up.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Arm Lock Breaking Position Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is on top, one knee above his shoulder, one foot across his body, an elbow-to-elbow grip on one arm.
games.text: Top player: keep the bottom player pinned and his head covered, separate his hands, and move both grips to one arm. Bottom player: pull your arm free, or make the top player fall to his back and get to your knees.

win.text: wins by separating the hands and getting two connections on the wrist.
wins by freeing the arm, or by reversing.

games.reset: The win is the breaking position, not the break. No finish is shown. The tap is honored instantly, every time. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the position, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.

sessions.connection: On the mat you can name your own mistake in a round without blaming your partner. Owning your part of a rupture works the same way. It starts with separating your piece from theirs.
sessions.takeaway: Owning your part is the doorway to repair.

sessions.probingQuestion: What does it take for you to say sorry and mean it?

games.title: Hand Fight with Dual Win Conditions
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both hand fighting at the wrists, elbows, and head.
games.text: Win one of two ways: collect three touches in any mix, or get an underhook and close your hands around your partner's shoulders, body, or leg.

win.text: wins, whether by three touches or by the underhook plus closed hands.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Guard Recovery with Passing Resistance Game
games.start: The bottom player is lying on his side. The top player has passed the legs and is at his hips.
games.text: Bottom player: stay mobile on your side, stop the top player's hands from connecting, and get your legs back in front. Top player: lock your hands around the bottom player's waist, chest, or back to stop the recovery.

win.text: wins by recovering to any real guard position while staying mobile.
wins by locking his hands.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Figure Four, Reintroduction with Hand-to-Mat or Knuckles-Behind Win
games.start: The bottom player is in side control, chest to chest. The top player starts with a figure-four grip on one arm, under his elbow.
games.text: Top player: stay under the elbow, even if you lose the hand for a moment, and put the bottom player's palm flat on the mat or his knuckles behind his back. Bottom player: fight the grip directly and get the figure four out from under your elbow.

win.text: wins by palm to mat or knuckles behind the back.
wins by removing the figure four from under the elbow.

games.reset: Switch arms every time someone wins, and swap top and bottom too. The win is the hand to the mat, not the finish. No finish is shown.
games.note: The win here is the hand to the mat or behind the back, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.

sessions.connection: Resetting and rolling clean with someone right after a hard round is like squaring up with words. A real apology is the same kind of reset: you get back in instead of carrying the grudge.
sessions.takeaway: Real repair has parts, and now you can name them.

sessions.probingQuestion: Can you stay when leaving would be easier?

games.title: Underhook Multiple Connection Game
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker has an underhook. The defender has an overhook.
games.text: Attacker: move your partner, connecting at the head, waist, or leg, and turn every connection into a leg pick. Defender: use the overhook and your other hand to keep him away.

win.text: wins only by picking up a leg, from any connection.
wins by stopping him for 30 seconds.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Guard Retention Connection Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back, feet hooked between the top player's knees, one hand on his ankle. The top player is standing.
games.text: Bottom player: keep both feet hooked and at least one hand on the top player at all times, switching feet as needed. Top player: get both feet to the outside of the bottom player's legs and touch his body with a shin.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the connection.
wins by getting outside both legs and making shin-to-body contact.

games.reset: The bottom player holds no matter what. If the top player gets outside and connects, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Chest to Chest Under Elbows Maintenance
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest, both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: keep both elbows away from the bottom player's body, using any body part in place of your arms if you need to. Bottom player: get both elbows back to touch your own body, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps both elbows covered.
wins by getting both elbows to touch his body, or by making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player gets both elbows to his body, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.

sessions.connection: Staying with a hard partner on the mat instead of switching is commitment made physical. Staying in a hard relationship when leaving is easier is the same choice. Both build the muscle of not bailing on people.
sessions.note: Staying is the skill. But leaving a harmful relationship is not failure. This is never an all-or-nothing rule.
sessions.takeaway: Staying is a choice you can make on purpose. You just practiced it.

sessions.probingQuestion: What does repair cost you, and is it worth paying?

games.title: Hand Fight with Progression Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both hand fighting at the wrists, elbows, and head.
games.text: Win one of two ways: get under an elbow and hook on, or connect both hands around a leg and pick it up.

win.text: wins, whether by hooking under an elbow or by picking up a leg.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Open Guard Takedown and Escape Game
games.start: The top player stands. The bottom player is on his back, fully connected, hands on the top player's ankles, feet inside his legs.
games.text: Bottom player: stay connected while putting the top player down on his hips or hands, then stand up, or stay connected as he rises. Top player: break the connections and make shin contact to pass.

win.text: wins by putting the top player down and getting up to standing, or by putting him down a different way and rising to a connection.
wins with shin contact.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.

games.title: Figure Four Threat Introduction Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back, in side control, chest to chest. The top player is on top with a figure-four grip on one arm.
games.text: Top player: use the grip to reach a threat, winning by putting the bottom player's hand on the mat, his hand behind his back, or a precursor position. Bottom player: free your elbows and escape.

win.text: wins by any of those listed positions.
wins by getting both elbows free.

games.reset: The win is the figure-four grip or the precursor position, not the finish. No finish is shown. The tap is honored instantly, every time. Roles switch after every win.
games.note: The win here is the grip or the position, not the finish. No finish is demonstrated.

sessions.connection: Open rolling puts it all together: control, finish, tap, reset, in one flow. Repair works the same way in relationships. It costs pride and comfort, and you decide it's worth paying. This closes the Initiation and points to the Return.
sessions.takeaway: You made contact, took the friction, survived the rupture, and learned repair.
